_meta.note: History bar-building and week-grouping cases (BEHAVIOR-SPEC section 7). Expectations are ported from the Android reference implementation's passing unit tests. All times are epoch milliseconds.

bars.name: session bars derive start from reset and sort newest first
bars.why: The weekly record is filtered out when building session bars. Start is derived as reset minus the window length, never stored. Newest first.

bars.name: current open window merges in and sorts newest
bars.why: The still-open window becomes a bar alongside the logged ones and, being newest, sorts first.

bars.name: a logged record with the same reset as current does not double up
bars.why: De-duplication is by reset time. This is the real-world race: the window closes and gets logged while the UI still holds it as current.

bars.name: hitLimit is peak >= 99.5, not exactly 100
bars.why: The server rarely reports a clean 100, so the threshold is 99.5 inclusive. A bar at 99.4 must not read as exhausted.

weeks.name: weeks group by Monday and sort newest first
weeks.why: Wed the 15th and Fri the 17th share the week beginning Mon the 13th. Mon the 6th is its own week and is already a Monday, so it maps to itself.

weeks.name: grouping uses the local zone, not UTC
weeks.why: Both instants are within six hours of each other but fall in different ISO weeks for a user in IST. A client that hard-codes UTC would put them in the same week. Monday is ISO day 1.

retention.why: Raw samples are kept 8 days so the 7-day window always has a full curve; closed windows are kept 366 days for the history bars. Prune on every write.
